forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Havant discovers £16.6m in unlawful emergency accommodation payments made without contracts
news_drafts.lead: Havant's Cabinet approved a remedial action plan on 23 September after discovering that between 2019/20 and July 2026 the council made approximately £16.6 million in payments to emergency accommodation providers without written contracts or proper procurement authority. The Statutory Officers' report found no evidence of compliant procurement procedures and no documented approval to make the payments. About £13.6 million of the total was paid from 2022/23 onwards, peaking at £3.8 million in 2024/25. The council is undertaking a comprehensive review of emergency accommodation arrangements and strengthening financial controls to prevent further unauthorised expenditure above prescribed thresholds. A council-wide assurance review of all procurement and contractual arrangements with third-party providers will report findings to the Governance Committee.

findings.headline: Study phase cost estimates on Conigar and Northney flood risk schemes are higher than originally assumed
findings.detail: Cost estimates for early-stage study work on two major flood and habitat schemes have been reviewed and found higher than planned. Conigar's 2026/27 budget now shows £305k estimated costs versus £50k existing approved budget. Northney shows £412k estimated costs versus £70k. If study costs are escalating in early phases, further cost increases are likely as schemes progress to detailed design and delivery.
findings.matters: Cost inflation in early project stages indicates likely further overruns as schemes move through design and delivery, affecting the council's ability to deliver its capital programme within budget
findings.figures: Conigar £7.95m lifetime (study estimate £305k); Northney £20.75m lifetime (study estimate £412k)
findings.quote: Cost estimates for Study Stage have been reviewed and are higher than originally assumed. Aim to receive approval by November 2026.  2026/27 budget therefore shows existing approved budget of £70k plus estimated costs for this f/y budget for the Study (412k).

findings.headline: Temporary accommodation refurbishment costs are escalating due to material and contractor cost inflation
findings.detail: The council is refurbishing two temporary accommodation properties at Stockheath Road and London Road. Design estimates for Stockheath Road now predict works may exceed budget, with rising material and contractor costs cited as the cause. The council is seeking alternative estimates and considering a phased approach to contain costs. This affects the £2.7m purchase budget and £448k fit-out budget.
findings.matters: A lender must monitor whether capital investments encounter cost pressures that could affect programme delivery and financial sustainability, particularly for housing services under pressure nationally
findings.figures: Purchase of TA £2,700k lifetime, Fit out £448k lifetime
findings.quote: Based on one design company estimate predicted works for Stockheath Road may be higher than budgeted (London Road cost estimate expected by E/O Aug). Causes include the rise of material and contractor costs over recent years.

findings.headline: The Broadmarsh coastal defence scheme faces seven-month design delays with regulatory risks that could require additional funding
findings.detail: The Broadmarsh scheme (£1.258m budget) experienced a seven-month delay to detailed design completion (from March 2026 to December 2026) due to Ground Investigation procurement delays and Flood Risk Activity Permit requirements. The council identifies two main risks: regulators may reject the proposed design approach requiring costlier alternatives, and the three-year construction deadline may be missed if construction funding is not secured. The project has no contingency allowance built in.
findings.matters: A lender needs confidence that major infrastructure projects will be delivered on schedule and budget; this scheme shows material delays, design uncertainty, and potential funding gaps
findings.figures: £1,258 budget, 7 month delay, spend to date £479,600, estimated outturn £1,039,655
findings.quote: The detailed design completion date had to move from March 2026 to December 2026 due to GI procurement and onsite delays, These were related to the necessity of Flood Risk Activity Permits (FRAP) for the investigations. This 7 month delay impacts the end date

findings.headline: The £79.9m Eastoke flood and coastal erosion scheme cannot proceed without unsecured Environment Agency Grant in Aid funding
findings.detail: The Eastoke scheme is budgeted at £79.907m over its lifetime. The FCERM7 business case is expected to be submitted in late summer 2026, with the outcome unclear until late autumn or early winter 2026. The council explicitly states the project cannot develop unless EA Grant in Aid funding is secured.
findings.matters: A lender must understand whether the council's capital programme depends on external funding that may not materialise, as this affects financial sustainability
findings.figures: £79,907 lifetime budget; outcome unclear until late autumn/early winter 2026
findings.quote: Development of the project will be subject to securing Environment Agency Grant in Aid funding. If no funding is secured then the project will not progress.

findings.headline: Financial sustainability and excessive financial pressure are identified as the council's highest-scoring corporate risk.
findings.detail: The corporate risk register highlights concerns regarding the council's financial sustainability, with the risk of excessive financial pressure identified as the highest-scoring risk. Mitigation measures include timely and accurate reporting of the forecast position, as reflected in this quarterly report.
findings.matters: When a council identifies financial sustainability as its highest-scoring risk, it signals management's awareness of severe financial distress.
findings.figures: Excessive financial pressure identified as highest-scoring risk on corporate risk register
findings.quote: The corporate risk register already highlights concerns regarding the Council's financial sustainability. The risk of excessive financial pressure remains the highest-scoring risk
